# Systems Thinking — Founding Fuel: Dense Observations (Batch 1, 2017–2025)

---

## REPEATED ARGUMENTS FF MAKES ON THIS THEME

**The world is complex and dynamic, not mechanical or predictable**
- "Ours is no longer an evolving world, but a mutating one. What we are witnessing now is change of the kind unprecedented in human history." — SOURCE: "Lessons from a mutating world" by Founding Fuel (2017-05-28)
- "No single model—simple or complex—can capture the dynamic complexity of this world... the world is made up of a variety of people, and they interact with each other in many different ways. These feedback loops keep the world dynamic and complex." — SOURCE: "Models, tech platforms and the hope for a better future" by Founding Fuel (2017-12-11)
- "Old economics policy frameworks view the world as a machine... But the world of humans is a complex, self-adapting system and must be examined from a different framework." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #380: Reading between the lines" by Founding Fuel (2021-05-25)

**Side effects are not side effects — they are effects of system blindness**
- Goleman/Sterman: "'In a system there are no side effects—just effects, anticipated or not. What we see as "side effects" simply reflect our flawed understanding of the system.'" — SOURCE: "FF Insights #703: System blindness" by Founding Fuel (2022-10-08)
- Gall's Law example on Aswan Dam: "Egyptian fields must now be artificially fertilized. Gigantic fertilizer plants have been built... The plants require enormous amounts of electricity. The dam must operate at capacity merely to supply the increased need for electricity which was created by the building of the dam." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #308: How systems fail" by Founding Fuel (2021-02-26)
- The seaside town rehabilitation centre story: "The solution had passed problems onto residents and visitors. The situation had become even messier than before." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #538: Do travel bans help?" by Founding Fuel (2021-12-02)

**Complex problems require systems thinking, not narrow specialisation**
- "Strong actions focused on only one part of an interconnected system can have large unintended consequences on other parts of the system." — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #183: Facts are better than dreams" by Founding Fuel (2020-09-22)
- "An abundance of experts has become a problem because they are too narrowly focused on separate pieces of the system." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #380: Reading between the lines" by Founding Fuel (2021-05-25)
- "Specialisation within the sciences has enabled great advances in many fields. However, the largest breakthroughs often create the greatest hazards in other areas because the impacts of narrow solutions on the whole system are not understood." — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #183: Facts are better than dreams" by Founding Fuel (2020-09-22)

**Top-down, centralised command-and-control does not work for systemic problems**
- "When confronted with large-scale problems, the default theory of effective management, of command-and-control, becomes very tempting to apply. Governments construct centralised, top-down programmes... This approach does not work because problems such as persistent poverty and inequality, environmental degradation, etc., are systemic issues." — SOURCE: "Local Systems Solutions: A framework for solving urban challenges" by Swati Ramanathan (2019-09-19) [repeating Arun Maira's note]
- "Efficiencies come from economies of scope—from a variety of local solutions rather than from centralized scale." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #380: Reading between the lines" by Founding Fuel (2021-05-25)
- India's lockdown: "Mumbai and Vietnam, among a few others, have demonstrated that a more effective way to deal with a multi-faceted problem with limited resources is to disperse responsibility so that appropriate local solutions can be found by stakeholders within communities." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #380: Reading between the lines" by Founding Fuel (2021-05-25)

**Gall's Law: complex systems must evolve from simple working systems**
- "A complex system that works is invariably found to have evolved from a simple system that worked. A complex system designed from scratch never works and cannot be patched up to make it work. You have to start over with a working simple system." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #308: How systems fail" by Founding Fuel (2021-02-26)
- But FF immediately complicates this: the microcredit crisis showed even "simple" products can fail systemically for users who don't have steady income. — SOURCE: "FF Daily #308: How systems fail" by Founding Fuel (2021-02-26)

**Cause and effect are distant in time and space in complex systems**
- Sterman: "Much of the time, people attribute what happens to them to events close in time and space, when in reality it's the result of the dynamics of the larger system within which they are embedded." — SOURCE: "FF Insights #703: System blindness" by Founding Fuel (2022-10-08)

**The answer lies at intersections, not in silos**
- "Who is to know in what silo, in whose head, or the intersection of what discipline pointers to answers may lie in." — SOURCE: "Lessons from a mutating world" by Founding Fuel (2017-05-28)
- Watson example: "The budding ornithologist would go on to study chemistry and then make landmark breakthroughs in genetics because he had read a paper on biology by a quantum physicist. Think about it!" — SOURCE: "FF Daily #342: How all things are interconnected" by Founding Fuel (2021-04-08)

**Systems change requires building chains of cause and effect, not single-variable explanations**
- In aviation crash investigation context: "No single clue—not the RAT, not the landing gear, not the shallow climb—explains AI 171 in isolation. The truth lies in connecting these events in the right sequence, proving how one failure triggered the next." — SOURCE: "Part 3: Unraveling AI 171: The Search for What Really Went Wrong" by Anmol Shrivastava (2025-06-29)

## FF'S INDIA-SPECIFIC ANGLE

**India as a site for systems-level experiments — Aadhaar, Swachh Bharat, healthcare**
- Aadhaar described as a platform experiment requiring systems thinking; Shankar Maruwada's shift from engineering/mechanistic thinking to dynamic, cross-disciplinary thinking explicitly driven by lessons from Aadhaar implementation. — SOURCE: "How may Einstein have thought of God and Aadhaar?" by Charles Assisi (2017-10-04)
- Swachh Bharat as requiring "a marriage of technology and civic participation" and systems understanding, not just top-down mandates. — SOURCE: "Models, tech platforms and the hope for a better future" by Founding Fuel (2017-12-11)
- Nandan Nilekani taking the concept of digital platforms from tech world into politics/bureaucracy as a live systems experiment. — SOURCE: "Models, tech platforms and the hope for a better future" by Founding Fuel (2017-12-11)

**India as "graveyard of successful pilots" — scaling failure**
- "India is a classic case of 'graveyard of successful pilots'. There are countless examples of pilot projects or micro-level efforts which work very well, but fail to scale." — SOURCE: "Purpose-Driven Networks: Sustaining large-scale movements of change" by Kiran Karnik (2019-10-02)
- Contrast with business startups scaling, but noting societal problems cannot be dealt with piecemeal or siloed. — SOURCE: "Purpose-Driven Networks" by Kiran Karnik (2019-10-02)

**India's health system as a canonical systems failure**
- India's DALY Rate of ~35,000 ranks 114th among 176 countries, just ahead of Rwanda which spends half as much, and 60 levels behind China. No state government since 1947 has shown inclination to increase health budgets near what is needed. — SOURCE: "Local Systems Solutions: A way for India to provide universal healthcare" by Nachiket Mor (2019-09-20)
- Detailed line-item budgets in India's health system "leaving little room for local autonomy and enterprise" identified as root systemic failure. — SOURCE: "Local Systems Solutions: A way for India to provide universal healthcare" by Nachiket Mor (2019-09-20)
- Thailand's health model (since 1970s: massive budget increases + successful local systems) held up as contrast. — SOURCE: "Local Systems Solutions: A way for India to provide universal healthcare" by Nachiket Mor (2019-09-20)

**India's urban transformation as systems challenge**
- Garbage as "a classic 'systems' problem" — with four interrelated themes (urban planning and design, capacities and resources, political representation, transparency and participation). — SOURCE: "Local Systems Solutions: A framework for solving urban challenges" by Swati Ramanathan (2019-09-19)
- Ramanathan's framework ("city systems") described as emerging from 20 years of practitioner experience in Indian urban transformation — not from theory. — SOURCE: "Local Systems Solutions: A framework for solving urban challenges" by Swati Ramanathan (2019-09-19)

**Indian Constitution's provisions on local governance as systems design**
- "The need for empowering local governance is often touted. For example, it is enshrined in the Indian Constitution through specific amendments." — SOURCE: "Local Systems Solutions: A framework for solving urban challenges" by Swati Ramanathan (2019-09-19)

**Data and India Stack as a structural feedback loop**
- "Right now, much of the debate in our country is around how the government will handle the data it collects—as a result of digitisation that Aadhaar and India Stack promise to catalyse." — SOURCE: "Is there a structural limit to growth?" by Founding Fuel (2017-07-02)

**Nagaland's women in politics as a systems problem**
- Customary law, tribal bodies, and state government interact to produce zero women elected to Nagaland assembly since 1963. "Enacting laws and lip service alone won't move the needle much." — SOURCE: "FF Insights #703: System blindness" by Founding Fuel (2022-10-08)

**Village health as exhibiting IoT — Inter-connectedness of Things**
- "Dealing with health problems in villages, one quickly understood the links between underweight children... and public safety, gender issues and caste discrimination... all because 'lower' castes were barred from drawing comparatively safer water from the village well." — SOURCE: "Purpose-Driven Networks" by Kiran Karnik (2019-10-02)

## FRAMEWORKS, THINKERS, AND MENTAL MODELS APPEARING REPEATEDLY

**Peter Senge / The Fifth Discipline (1990)**
- "Systems thinking, a framework that helps us take a helicopter view of a problem... A key idea in the book suggests that there are structural limits to growth." Reinforcing and balancing loops. — SOURCE: "Is there a structural limit to growth?" by Founding Fuel (2017-07-02)

**Fritjof Capra / The Systems View of Life**
- "The major problems of our time... cannot be understood in isolation. They are systemic problems... Ultimately, these problems must be seen as just different facets of one single crisis, which is largely a crisis of perception." — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #100: A systems view" by Founding Fuel (2020-07-01)

**Arun Maira / Transforming Systems** (recurring anchor figure across multiple pieces)
- His framework for "Local Systems Solutions" spans at least two full articles and his themes recur in multiple daily digests. He contrasts command-and-control with networked, locally adaptive systems. — SOURCE: "Local Systems Solutions: A framework for solving urban challenges" (2019-09-19); "Local Systems Solutions: A way for India to provide universal healthcare" (2019-09-20); "Purpose-Driven Networks" (2019-10-02); "WFH Daily #183" (2020-09-22); "FF Daily #380" (2021-05-25)

**John Gall / Systemantics: How Systems Work and Especially How They Fail**
- Gall's Law: complex systems must evolve from simple working systems. Examples: insecticides creating immunity, Aswan Dam paradox. — SOURCE: "FF Daily #308: How systems fail" by Founding Fuel (2021-02-26)

**Daniel Goleman / Focus: The Hidden Driver of Excellence**
- John Sterman's systems thinking framework; "side effects" as symptoms of system blindness; cause-and-effect distance in complex systems. — SOURCE: "FF Insights #703: System blindness" by Founding Fuel (2022-10-08); also cited in "FF Daily #380" (2021-05-25)

**John Gribbin / Deep Simplicity: Chaos, Complexity and the Emergence of Life**
- "A complex system is really just a system that is made up of several simpler components interacting with one another." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #413: How to think of complex systems" by Founding Fuel (2021-07-03)

**John Sterman (MIT Sloan) — explicit named expert on systems thinking**
- "'It's insidious,' says Sterman. 'You get short-term relief, and then the problem comes back, often worse than before.'" — SOURCE: "FF Insights #703: System blindness" by Founding Fuel (2022-10-08)

**Rosalind Armson / Growing on the Way: Systems Thinking for Messy Situations**
- The seaside town rehabilitation centre story as canonical example of second-order consequences. — SOURCE: "FF Daily #538: Do travel bans help?" by Founding Fuel (2021-12-02)

**Feedback loops as core analytical unit**
- Reinforcing loops (virtuous cycle of sales → satisfaction → more sales) and balancing/counter loops as the architecture of all systems. — SOURCE: "Is there a structural limit to growth?" by Founding Fuel (2017-07-02); "Models, tech platforms" (2017-12-11)

**Seelos, Farley & Rose / Stanford Social Innovation Review — Systems Change principles**
- Broad, Hidden, Creates possibilities, Adaptive explorations, Vision-oriented, Managing risk by making smaller bets, MERL. — SOURCE: "FF Daily #276: The danger of single story" by Founding Fuel (2021-01-19)

**Chimamanda Adichie — "The Danger of a Single Story"**
- Used as a systems epistemology point: multiple perspectives necessary to avoid single-story bias in understanding systems. — SOURCE: "FF Daily #276: The danger of single story" by Founding Fuel (2021-01-19)

**Jim Collins / Good to Great — Stockdale Paradox**
- Unwavering faith + confronting brutal facts = Churchill's Statistical Office model. Juxtaposed with systems thinking challenge of seeing the full picture. — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #183: Facts are better than dreams" by Founding Fuel (2020-09-22)

**Timothy Wilson / Redirect — Perceptual bias in interpreting reality**
- Duck/rabbit and THE/MAT examples as visual demonstration that context shapes interpretation of the same data. — SOURCE: "FF Daily #276: The danger of single story" by Founding Fuel (2021-01-19)

**Aviation crash investigation as systems thinking in action**
- Chain-of-causation methodology: "Every scenario investigators explore isn't about isolated guesses—it's about building complete chains of cause and effect, then testing whether each element holds up." — SOURCE: "Part 3: Unraveling AI 171" by Anmol Shrivastava (2025-06-29)

**Shankar Maruwada / EkStep & Aadhaar — practitioner systems thinker**
- Shift from mechanistic/engineering frame to dynamic, cross-disciplinary synthesis: "Why cannot we push ourselves instead to think dynamically and across disciplines instead?" — SOURCE: "How may Einstein have thought of God and Aadhaar?" by Charles Assisi (2017-10-04)

**Haresh Chawla — optionality and platform feedback loops**
- "The optionality resides in the habit they can create and whether the teams have the vision to expand into adjacencies." Systems logic applied to tech platform value. — SOURCE: "Is there a structural limit to growth?" by Founding Fuel (2017-07-02)
